sections: Custom Pen and Ink Home Portraits, Quality Reproductions and Commissions

Your home tells a story of milestones, memories, and moments worth preserving. Whether it's the family home, a cozy cottage, or your beachside holiday home, each building portrait is hand-drawn with care using traditional pencil and ink techniques and a keen eye for detail.
Artist Alison Greenway brings architecture to life with precision and heart, transforming your reference photos into a work of art you'll treasure forever.
Custom drawings can also be commissioned to feature your workplace building, business, office, stable complex, hotel or restaurant - these can be Tax Deductible.

Perfect for Gifting These portraits make ideal gifts for holidays, birthdays, anniversaries, weddings, retirements, housewarming parties, and for new homeowners or anyone who appreciates art. Gift Vouchers are also available.
Original Art Ownership You will own a physical piece of original art, a lasting treasure that captures the essence of your home.
Certificate of Authenticity You will receive a Certificate to verify your artwork's originality, provenance, and value, offering you assurance.
100% Hand-Drawn Art Meticulously crafted using quality COPIC Multi Liner pens and DERWENT Graphic pencils, Graphic Tint and Watercolour pencils, ensuring a unique, and authentic touch.
Personalised Features Tailored to reflect your home’s distinctive characteristics and landscaping, making every portrait one-of-a-kind.
No Digital Tricks My work is free from AI, filters, or digital alterations. It's about true craftsmanship and artistry.
Progress Updates You will receive updates throughout the creation process, allowing you to witness your artwork come to life step by step.
Commissioned artwork is a thoughtful way to celebrate life’s special moments. A detailed house portrait captures memories that last a lifetime.

Alison Greenway is a dedicated artist based in Toowoomba, specialising in custom house portraits and commissioned artwork across Queensland. Her pieces are known for their warmth, detail, and personal touch — making them perfect gifts for those you love.
A commissioned piece by Alison Greenway is more than art — it’s a lasting memory

blocks.text: House Portraits
Recreate an Image of Your Well Loved Home
Many people choose to commission a drawing of their favourite home or a property that holds years of family memories when they are downsizing, or relocating to another city or region.

A House Portrait can also be a wonderful gift for family members who live a long way from their family and the ‘family home’, it can help them to remember the great times they shared when they lived in the home - all together.

House Portraits also help to create a comfortable ambiance in offices and waiting rooms of organisations and private Practices, especially if you work long hours away from your family and much loved home.
A portrait of your Business premises may also work well as a form of marketing as it establishing an image for your business in the community.

Being a visual artist Alison understands the passion that we can have towards our homes, the efforts we put in to restore or modify them to suit our desires and lifestyle - she has renovated multiple homes over the years and has enjoyed the process from start to finish.
Contact Alison by phone or email to enquire about Commissioning an Artwork process

Art commission means engaging an artist to create artwork specifically for you. Alison can create a personalised and unique drawing or painting of your house to hang in your home or to give to your loved ones. Call Alison to discuss timelines and options available.

Your commissioned artwork is guaranteed to be a ‘one of a kind’, and it will not only remind you of your beautiful home but the wonderful memories that have been created in the home over the years. You will also receive a Certificate of Authenticity on delivery of your personalised drawing.

blocks.text: Step 3: Arrange deposit and email order form

blocks.text: Step 4: The Proof

blocks.text: Inspired by architectural design and historical heritage
Alison Greenway

Alison has resided in the Darling Downs region of Southern Queensland for almost 25 years, enjoying life as she mixes the peaceful countryside with her passion for drawing and showcasing the unique architectural buildings found throughout Queensland.

She is a Commission Artist who loves to draw homes for others, and those who also share her passion for charming and stylish buildings. Her skills initially developed when she did 4 years of Technical Drawing studies when at school, she has continued to refine these skills over many years and focussed on detailed drawings of quality properties.
Her motivation is to create drawings that celebrate and respect each homes heritage and presence, and associated memories for the families who commission a ‘one off individual piece’ of art.

Alison predominantly uses black and coloured inks, pencil, and watercolour; drawings are available in 3 sizes – A5, A4 and A3. She has a number of Limited Addition quality Giclee Prints on cotton rag paper available for sale on this website.

/the-bull-and-barley-inn-cambooya.heading: The Bull and Barley Inn Cambooya
/the-bull-and-barley-inn-cambooya.lead: As an artist who is both passionate and motivated to recreate the details of unique architectural buildings found throughout Queensland, I was challenged to draw this beautiful and historical building especially as it is found on ‘my doorstep’ being so close to Toowoomba my home city.
/the-bull-and-barley-inn-cambooya.imageAlt: Toowoomba Artist Alison Greenway was commissioned to create a portrait of The Bull and Barley Inn Cambooya.

blocks.text: The Bull and Barley Inn is in the picturesque township of Cambooya which is part of the Darling Downs in Southern Queensland. This stunning building has a rich history dating back to 1902, when it was originally established as the Cambooya Railway Hotel.

Initially one of three hotels in the town, it became the sole remaining hotel and was renamed the Bull and Barley Inn in 1978. This two-story building with a restaurant and accommodation, is known for its historic charm and is a popular destination for both locals and tourists.
Some interesting facts about this Classic Country Inn
blocks.html: Some interesting facts about this Classic Country Inn

items: 1902: The Inn opens as the Cambooya Railway Hotel, serving as a railway station and general store.
Early Years: It was one of three pubs in Cambooya but eventually became the only one remaining.
1978: The name was changed to the Bull and Barley Inn.
2017: The Inn was restored immaculately when it underwent major restorations which included a new roof, electrical rewiring and upgraded plumbing.

The Bull and Barley Inn is known throughout the region for its decorative two-story building, wide verandahs, and historic charm. It features an old-world atmosphere, with displays of original photographs and memorabilia adorning its walls – paying tribute to the hotel’s local history
Cambooya is located in the region of the late author Steele Rudd, creator of the well-known Australian characters, Dad ‘n’ Dave.

A local treasure and well patronised waterhole receive visitors from far and wide; it is a thriving business and provides over 1,000 meals a week, being so popular that it is wise to book to get a table.

blocks.text: A custom house portrait captures more than walls and windows, it preserves emotion, history, memories and pride in a deeply personal way.

Whether it's a first home, a forever home, or one that’s part of your family legacy, a hand-drawn house portrait offers a tangible way to celebrate it. It tells a story. Every line drawn in ink represents the character, detail, and feeling that photos often miss. It's a keepsake that holds meaning, and it only becomes more valuable with time.
A personalised House Portrait Drawing is ideal for so many reasons; clients have commissioned me to do drawings for many purposes, events and gift ideas including:

items: Christmas – Surprise a loved one on Christmas morning with a thoughtful gift.
Father’s Day / Mother’s Day – A special gift for those who have ‘everything’.
Weddings – A beautiful way to celebrate the first home a couple shares.
Anniversaries – A lasting tribute to decades of shared memories.
New Home Purchases – Love and thoughtful unexpected housewarming gift
Downsizing – A way to take a lifetime of memories when you relocate.
Retirement Gift – A loving reminder and keepsake from work colleagues.

blocks.text: Here is a list of why some people have contacted me from all over Queensland, and why they commissioned a hand drawn House Portrait especially for them.
Fred and Dorothy moved their old business to new premises.

This lovely couple have operated their business from a heritage listed property for over 20 years, and they were in the process of building a purpose built complex and relocating their old business to it. They both shared a lot of sentimental feelings, along with their many long term and loyal customers for the older building. As a nod of respect, they commissioned me to draw the ‘old building’, and it now hangs proudly in their new business showroom for all to see.
Dylan’s gift for his Partner’s Birthday

Dylan and Sussan have lived in North Queensland for the past 10 years in a rented Queenslander home, recently they have decided to relocate to Brisbane for employment opportunities for Dylan and to be close to their family members. Sussan was a little reluctant and sad to move from her home as she loved the character of the home and the many memories that had been made there. Dylan decided to have this beautiful property drawn so contacted me by text to commission a House Portrait Drawing to give it to Sussan for a Birthday gift just before they were to leave for Brisbane. Sussan was delighted and has framed the drawing and hangs it affectionately on their dining room wall so all the family and friends can see it.
Jackie misses her First Home

After having several very successful years Jackie and her Husband decided to upscale and purchase a new home that offered more space for their growing family. Although they really loved their modest Queensland cottage, and it had so many memories as their children were growing they felt a need to sell and buy a larger and more centrally located home that suited their changing needs better. Jackie and her family love their new home but wanted to have a memento of their first home to remember the early fun years as their family grew. Jackie contacted me to do a House Portrait Drawing to keep these treasured memories alive.

Jessie and Sam run a small tourism business in a medium sized country town in Southern Queensland. They called me and asked me to do a commissioned drawing of their quaint ‘country cottage’ so they could feature it in their recently renovated indoor garden room at the back of their coffee house. Since falling in love with their completed drawing they worked with me further to organise a professionally photographed image of the drawing – they now sell quality print reproductions and postcards of their Coffee House to tourists in their region.

Amanda has been travelling and living overseas for many years, earlier this year to her families delight she decided to move back to Toowoomba her hometown to resettle. After purchasing her very first home, a cute cottage hidden behind an established garden her family wanted to commemorate this new stage in Amanda’s life. They commissioned me to do a House Portrait Drawing of Amanda’s home so they could surprise her at her housewarming party, they felt it was the perfect way to express their love and excitement that she is now settling down and back home with them.

body: Whether it's a first home, a forever home, or one that’s part of your family legacy, a hand-drawn house portrait offers a tangible way to celebrate it. It tells a story. Every line drawn in ink represents the character, detail, and feeling that photos often miss. It's a keepsake that holds meaning, and it only becomes more valuable with time.
A personalised House Portrait Drawing is ideal for so many reasons; clients have commissioned me to do drawings for many purposes, events and gift ideas including:
Here is a list of why some people have contacted me from all over Queensland, and why they commissioned a hand drawn House Portrait especially for them.

This lovely couple have operated their business from a heritage listed property for over 20 years, and they were in the process of building a purpose built complex and relocating their old business to it. They both shared a lot of sentimental feelings, along with their many long term and loyal customers for the older building. As a nod of respect, they commissioned me to draw the ‘old building’, and it now hangs proudly in their new business showroom for all to see.

Dylan and Sussan have lived in North Queensland for the past 10 years in a rented Queenslander home, recently they have decided to relocate to Brisbane for employment opportunities for Dylan and to be close to their family members. Sussan was a little reluctant and sad to move from her home as she loved the character of the home and the many memories that had been made there. Dylan decided to have this beautiful property drawn so contacted me by text to commission a House Portrait Drawing to give it to Sussan for a Birthday gift just before they were to leave for Brisbane. Sussan was delighted and has framed the drawing and hangs it affectionately on their dining room wall so all the family and friends can see it.
